summary: kepler pulls unpinned tarball with install script from non-registry host at install time
details: package.json declares a single dependency `flag-serial-object-syntax` pinned to the URL `https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax` on a non-npm host, with no version, tag, or integrity hash. The shrinkwrap marks that dependency `hasInstallScript: true`, so `npm install kepler` fetches whatever bytes that mutable URL currently serves and executes its lifecycle scripts on the installer's machine. The visible `kepler` tarball is a hollow shim: `index.js` exports `version: "1.0.0"` while the package is published as `1.999.999`, metadata is placeholder (author "Package Registry", repo `github.com/example/kepler`, description "Generated package"), and the 1.999.999 version is a dependency-confusion tactic designed to outrank internal versions of any `kepler` name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
